title: Foundations: Entertainment Arts Data Types
summary: What entertainment arts data types are and why shared schemas matter.
body:
Data types for shows, venues, artworks, and rights: the business records behind the performance.

Shared data types let every system in entertainment arts exchange records without translation errors. This database defines the core entities — each with fields, types, a real example, and the standard it follows. Use the type-definition records to design, and the schema records to build.

title: Performance - Type Definition
summary: Field-level definition of Performance for entertainment arts.
body:
Performance: One show on one date.

FIELDS:
- perf_id (string): ID
- work_id (string): FK to Work
- venue_id (string): FK
- date (date): ISO 8601
- time (string): HH:MM
- capacity (number): Seats
- sold (number): Tickets sold

EXAMPLE:
{
 "perf_id": "PF-77120",
 "work_id": "W-HAM",
 "venue_id": "V-RICHARD",
 "date": "2026-10-02",
 "time": "19:30",
 "capacity": 1319,
 "sold": 1298
}

STANDARD: Ticketing practice. Every record of this type should carry these fields with these meanings — that consistency is what makes data interoperable across entertainment arts systems.

title: Performance - Schema and Validator
summary: JSON schema and a working Python validator for Performance.

program.code:
# Performance: dataclass + validator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

@dataclass
class Performance:
    perf_id: str = None  # ID
    work_id: str = None  # FK to Work
    venue_id: str = None  # FK
    date: str = None  # ISO 8601
    time: str = None  # HH:MM
    capacity: float = None  # Seats
    sold: float = None  # Tickets sold

REQUIRED = ["perf_id", "work_id", "venue_id", "date"]

def validate(rec: dict) -> list:
    errors = []
    for f in REQUIRED:
        if f not in rec or rec[f] is None:
            errors.append(f'missing: {f}')
    return errors

sample = {'perf_id': 'PF-77120', 'work_id': 'W-HAM', 'venue_id': 'V-RICHARD', 'date': '2026-10-02', 'time': '19:30', 'capacity': 1319, 'sold': 1298}
print('validation errors:', validate(sample))
print('record ok:', not validate(sample))
program.note: Dataclass plus a validator for required fields; runs as-is.
